params.body:
What naviskore's CI has and this one did not. The job structure stays as it was (`up-to-date`,
`phpunit` on MariaDB, `assets`); these are four new jobs beside it, each answering one question, so
a red cross says which one. They run next to the suite and cost a minute or two each.

| job | what it asks | where it stands today |
|---|---|---|
| `audit` | does the dependency tree carry a new advisory | composer clean, npm at a ceiling of 13 |
| `lint` | do the front-end modules lint | 31 warnings, ceiling 31 |
| `style` | is the PHP this branch changed formatted | green |
| `static` | does the analysis find anything new | level 5, 2.058 in the baseline |

**`npm audit --audit-level=high` is not what the job runs, and that is deliberate.** The tree
carries twelve high and one critical advisory today: nearly all of them come from
`tui-image-editor`, which drags its own `webpack`, `tar` and `chokidar` along, plus `axios`, still
on `^0.19` against a current 1.20. The flag would make the job red on the day it lands, and a check
that is red on arrival teaches people to look away from red. So the same shape as the ESLint
ceiling you asked for: `.github/scripts/npm-audit-ceiling.mjs` fails when the count rises, says so
when it falls, and the day it reaches zero the script is replaced by the flag. `composer audit` has
nothing to forgive and runs as itself.

**Pint runs on the diff, not the repository.** Pint disagrees with 864 of the files here, which is
what a codebase looks like after years under a style bot that stopped reporting (`.styleci.yml` is
still in the tree; no StyleCI check has run on a pull request since the takeover). Formatting all
of them in one commit would collide with every open pull request and take the history of every file
with it. So `pint --test --diff=origin/main`: new and touched code is formatted, the rest waits
until it is touched, and the check can only improve. `pint.json` carries the same preset and the
same exception as `.styleci.yml` did, so nothing about the house style changes.

**PHPStan found two dead controllers on its first run.** `RegisterController` and
`VerificationController` use `Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\RegistersUsers` and `VerifiesEmails`,
traits that left the framework with `laravel/ui`. Neither is routed anywhere, and registration goes
through the invitation flow now. PHPStan refuses to put an unknown trait in a baseline, and it is
right: the classes would fatal the moment anything touched them. They are gone.

**Infection is its own workflow**, weekly on Monday morning and on demand, with the report as an
artifact, a two-hour ceiling, and `--only-covered` because coverage here is about a quarter and
mutating the rest would make thousands of mutants nobody can kill. No MSI threshold: the first run
is the measurement, and a number to hold comes after it.

Two things the new jobs surfaced that are not fixed here, both worth their own look:
`session.js:91` assigns `window.location.href` to itself (that was meant to be a reload), and
`axios@0.19` is four majors behind with an SSRF advisory against it.

**What #669 got wrong.** Two mechanical mistakes in the new jobs, both fixed here. `composer audit`
was run in a job that never installs anything, and without a vendor directory it wants `--locked` to
read the lock file instead. And `composer install` runs `package:discover` in its
`post-autoload-dump` hook, which boots the application and needs the directories the framework
writes in; the `phpunit` job makes them before installing, and the two new PHP jobs did not.

**Order:** #668 also touches `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, and the gateway pushes snapshots rather
than diffs. Merge that one first; this one then goes red on `up-to-date` and I re-propose it
rebased.

Replaces #669.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: Four checks beside the tests, and a weekly mutation run (replaces #669)
